title: Linking Linear and Rotational Motion
short: A point at radius r moves with v = rω and tangential acceleration a = rα.
trouble: Students think every point on a spinning wheel moves at the same speed.

blocks.html: A spinning wheel has one angular velocity, yet its parts move at different speeds. Linking the two kinds of quantity explains why, and it ties turning to centripetal acceleration.

A point at radius $r$ that turns through $\Delta\theta$ travels the arc $\Delta s = r\Delta\theta$. Divide by the time: its speed is $v = \dfrac{\Delta s}{\Delta t} = r\dfrac{\Delta\theta}{\Delta t} = r\omega$. If $\omega$ changes, $v$ changes $r$ times as fast: the tangential acceleration is $\role[tangential acceleration]{acceleration}{a_t} = \role[distance from the axis]{position}{r}\role{angacc}{\alpha}$. And moving in a circle at speed $v$ always needs the centripetal acceleration $a_c = \dfrac{v^2}{r} = r\omega^2$, toward the center.

For a point at distance $r$ from the axis (angles in radians): speed $\role[speed]{velocity}{v} = \role[distance from the axis]{position}{r}\role{angvel}{\omega}$, tangential acceleration $\role[tangential acceleration]{acceleration}{a_t} = \role[distance from the axis]{position}{r}\role{angacc}{\alpha}$ (along the path), centripetal acceleration $\role[centripetal acceleration]{acceleration}{a_c} = \role[distance from the axis]{position}{r}\role{angvel}{\omega}^2$ (toward the center). All points share one $\omega$ and $\alpha$, but $v$, $a_t$ and $a_c$ grow with $r$.

blocks.title: Speed on a merry-go-round
blocks.q: A merry-go-round turns at $0.80\ \text{rad/s}$. How fast does a child $2.5\ \text{m}$ from the center move? And one $1.0\ \text{m}$ from the center?
steps: $v = (1.0)(0.80) = 0.80\ \text{m/s}$. Same $\omega$, but the outer child covers a bigger circle in the same time.

blocks.title: Accelerations of a rim point
blocks.q: A disk of radius $0.20\ \text{m}$ turns at $5.0\ \text{rad/s}$ and is speeding up at $8.0\ \text{rad/s}^2$. Find the tangential and centripetal accelerations of a rim point.
steps: $a_t = r\alpha = (0.20)(8.0) = 1.6\ \text{m/s}^2$, along the direction of motion.
They are at right angles, so the total is $\sqrt{1.6^2 + 5.0^2} = 5.2\ \text{m/s}^2$.

blocks.title: Linked by a belt
blocks.q: A belt joins a $5.0\ \text{cm}$ motor pulley turning at $1200$ rpm to a $20\ \text{cm}$ pulley. How fast does the big pulley turn?
steps: A belt that doesn't slip moves at one speed, so both rims have the same $v$: $r_1\omega_1 = r_2\omega_2$.

blocks.html: Thinking every point on a spinning wheel moves at the same speed. Every point has the same angular velocity, but its speed is $v = r\omega$: the hub barely moves while the rim races. Check with extremes: the point on the axle ($r = 0$) has $v = 0$.

blocks.cap: A point speeding up on a circle: the tangential part of its acceleration changes its speed, and the centripetal part turns its velocity.
